label: Remove
description: Staged feature/module removal: dependency impact scan, explicit strategy, teardown in reverse layer order, dead-code sweep, PR (no auto-merge). If you decide to use sub agents, always set openai-oauth/gpt-5.5 · effort: low.
when_to_use: Use when the task is to remove, drop, or deprecate existing functionality. Do NOT use for restructuring code that stays ('refactor') or for behaviour changes that keep the feature ('feature', 'bugfix').

guards.message: Complete the dependency scan, strategy decision, and staged teardown (tests green at every stage) before committing.
This workflow does NOT merge — verify the pre-push gate genuinely passed (never --no-verify), report the PR as ready, and stop.

steps.label: Dependency impact scan
steps.guidance: Read the issue, then map everything that touches the target before deleting anything: callers/consumers (grep the symbols), config keys, docs, tests, protocol/wire surfaces, and persisted data it owns. Record the full inventory with file:line — an unscanned consumer becomes a broken build or a silent behaviour change. Done when the inventory is written down.

steps.label: Choose the removal strategy
steps.guidance: Decide and record: hard delete (no external consumers, no persisted data concerns), deprecate-then-delete (external consumers need a migration window — define the window and the warning), or archive (data/docs retained, code removed). Note any wire-format or persistence compatibility the repo's conventions require you to keep. If consumers outside this repo exist and you cannot verify them, stop and flag it rather than guessing. Done when the strategy and its rationale are recorded.

steps.label: Staged teardown in reverse layer order
steps.guidance: Remove top-down through the architecture: interface first, then application, then infrastructure, then domain — so nothing ever references a deleted layer and the tree compiles at every stage. At each stage delete the layer's code AND its tests together, run the targeted tests, and only then descend. Update docs that referenced the feature as you go (repo_docs guard tests will catch stragglers). Done when the target is gone and targeted tests are green.

steps.label: Dead code and orphan sweep
steps.guidance: Hunt what the removal orphaned: helpers/types now unused (the strict clippy + machete gates catch most, but grep for the removed feature's vocabulary too), config keys nothing reads, feature-file scenarios for deleted behaviour, and stale doc references. Delete or file each one — an orphan left behind is half a removal. Done when the sweep result is recorded.

steps.label: Commit and push through the full gate
steps.guidance: Branch if on master, stage only intended deletions/changes, commit citing the issue and the chosen strategy. `git push` in the FOREGROUND and WAIT for the fast pre-push gate; fix failures and push again; never --no-verify. Done when the push exited with the gate passing.

steps.label: Open the PR
steps.guidance: Open the PR with `gh pr create`: body states what was removed, the strategy and why, the dependency inventory, and any migration/deprecation notes consumers need. Confirm OPEN state and head SHA via `gh pr view <n> --json number,headRefOid,state`. Done when PR number and head SHA are confirmed.

steps.label: Request authoritative CI and report the PR (no merge)
steps.guidance: After all review comments are resolved and the current head is final, run `gh pr edit <n> --add-label merge-requested`. This requests authoritative CI for that exact revision. Wait with `gh pr checks <n> --watch`; if another commit is pushed, the label is removed automatically and must be reapplied only when ready. Do NOT merge or set auto-merge; report the PR and CI result for human merge.
